gaps.text: In-line measurement of Melt temperature at the measurement point with temperature sensor at the probe

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (MIR ATR and Raman would share one measurement point, preferably through a combined probe rather than two separate ports. The two acquisitions run at different rates and must be aligned to a common time step, with block scaling so that neither block dominates the model. Each block keeps its own calibration, and the fused model must beat the best single-method model on independent runs, otherwise the second instrument is not worth keeping.)
An achievable MIR fiber length for a hot process installation; the sources give short laboratory cable examples for infrared fibers and long lengths only for silica.
Probe temperature and pressure ratings for a hot extruder interface.

items.finding: Temperature was varied together with concentrations and ionic strength to build a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests treating melt temperature at the probe as a variable to record and vary in robustness testing for the MIR ATR option, rather than assuming a fixed temperature.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is an aqueous acid liquid-liquid extraction study, not a hot polymer melt, and it does not describe a probe-integrated temperature sensor or its in-line performance.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E02 ¶19

items.finding: The review says each dataset's contribution and complementarity should be evaluated before fusing data from multiple sources.
items.how_it_applies: For the combined MIR ATR/Raman option, plan per-block contribution checks and compare the fused model against the best single method on independent runs before keeping the second instrument.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a general review statement, not a test on hot polymer melt or a specific MIR/Raman probe configuration.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E03 ¶82

items.finding: A Raman and FT-IR food analytical study is cited where instrument complementarity alone was not sufficient to improve prediction of several CQAs.
items.how_it_applies: This supports making the fused model prove itself against the best single-method model on independent runs; if it does not, the second instrument may not add value.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited case is food analysis, not polymer extrusion, and uses different instruments and CQAs; the result is a reason to test, not proof for this process.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E03 ¶36
